title: MACH Factory Event v3
description: One transition of the intake ledger, as a line of .factory/intake/events.jsonl. Events are written only when the ledger changes, in sequence order, so the log can be replayed but is never a second source of truth. Version 3 (M11): no wave_id or project_id; epic_id and issue say where a slice belongs (null when not known).

seq.description: Strictly increasing by one; a reader resumes from the last seq it saw.

source_commit.description: The integration-branch commit ready folders were last read from.

epic_id.description: The slice's epic (EPIC-NNN), when the event is about a slice.

issue.description: The slice's own GitHub issue number, when it came as an issue; it is also its ticket.

runner_id.description: The machine-local runner that was enabled when this was written; null when the Factory was not enabled.

execution_id.description: The supervisor's execution this event belongs to, if any.

source.description: Which part of MACH acted: an engineer's command, product intake, or the supervisor.

cause.description: The seq of the event that led to this one, where one is known.

refs.description: Where the authoritative state is kept, as paths in the project: the cell's cell.json, the execution's folder. An event describes a change; these say where to read the truth.

data.description: Details by type: problems (intake.refused), reasons (dependency.blocked), depends_on (dependency.resolved), commit (slice.integrated), stage, risk, branch, by (engineer, or the name of an authorized caller) and authorization (work.scheduled), from_revision and effect, and since M7 outcome (abandoned or superseded-in-work), why and by (revision.superseded); adopted, dependencies, and since M7 reissued and follows (slice.materialized), reason (human.required). Supervisor events: autonomy, limits and by (factory.*); from_commit and commit (revision.discovered); dispatched, started and held (scheduling.decided); stage, next and attempt (work.claimed); session_id, workflow, until and limits, and since M6.5 provenance (a snapshot of digests, versions and identifiers taken once at start, or null with provenance_reason capture-failed; see M6_1_EVENT_CONTRACT.md section 10.1.1) (execution.started); from_stage and stage (station.observed); kind (recovery.started); stage, next, waiting_for, how (exited, killed, interrupted, timed-out, could-not-start or unknown), exit_code (since M7), seen_to_end and cost_usd (execution.completed); how, claude_error, exit_code, attempt and, since M7, not_progressing (workflow-stuck or same-refusal) (execution.failed). Never a prompt, a command line, an environment variable or a credential.
